📌 Hidden Fees: Why “Zero Fee” Doesn’t Mean Free

Main Points
⏺ Crypto trade costs can hide in spreads, slippage, and execution routes
⏺ “No fee” often means the cost moves somewhere else
⏺ This post explains how to see the real price of an action

1️⃣ Spread — the gap between buy and sell price can already be your first hidden cost.
2️⃣ Slippage — weaker liquidity pushes your final price away from the quote.
3️⃣ Routing — an app or aggregator may choose a route that benefits it more than you.
4️⃣ Network Costs — even if the platform charges no fee, gas is still a real expense.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — compare final received amounts, check multiple routes, and don’t trust “0% fee” alone.

Final Thoughts

Trades are rarely free. If the fee isn’t visible in one line, it may live inside price, routing, or liquidity.

📌 Hyperliquid adds 10 HYPE rule as price falls to $78.98 

🔗 Hyperliquid has introduced revised order priority rules on its testnet, including a reported 10 HYPE delegation requirement for traders seeking faster order handling through its priority fee system. In an October 18 announcement circulated through its community channels, the decentralized derivatives platform outlined changes to write priority fees following feedback from users. The proposed rules concern traders who depend on low delays when placing, modifying or canceling orders.

🔖 The announcement identifies four changes involving account settings, transaction processing and eligibility for priority fees. Hyperliquid’s existing technical documentation confirms how its priority fee system operates, although the newly reported delegation threshold has not yet appeared in the publicly accessible documentation reviewed for this report. The changes are described as live on testnet. No confirmed date has been announced for applying the revised requirements to mainnet trading.

‼️ The October 18 update introduces a minimum delegated balance of 10 HYPE for accounts seeking to use IOC and ALO priority fees, according to the announcement. IOC, short for immediate-or-cancel, refers to an order that attempts immediate execution and cancels any portion that cannot be filled. ALO, or add-liquidity-only, is used to place orders that join the order book without immediately taking available liquidity.

Trump’s Approval Hits a New Low as Democrats Gain Ground Ahead of the Midterms


Trump is facing a growing political challenge just two weeks before the November midterm elections. 

His approval rating has fallen to a record low, economic anxiety is weighing on voters, and Democrats have opened a significant lead in the race for control of Congress, according to a new Washington Post–ABC News–Ipsos poll published October 18.

The numbers paint a difficult picture for the White House. Just 33% of Americans approve of Trump’s performance as president, while 66% disapprove. More than half of all adults surveyed, 52%, say they strongly disapprove of his leadership. 

The president’s approval rating has dropped four percentage points since July and eight points compared with the same period last year. Among likely voters, his approval stands at 38%, with 62% expressing disapproval.

For Democrats, the findings offer a potential opening ahead of the November 3 elections, when control of Congress will be at stake. The party leads Republicans by eight percentage points among likely voters in the congressional contest, with 52% supporting Democratic candidates compared with 44% backing Republicans. 

The gap has widened since the previous Washington Post poll in July, when Democrats held a three-point advantage among registered voters. Economic dissatisfaction appears to be one of the central factors behind the shift in public opinion. 

Rising gasoline prices, increasingly expensive groceries and mounting health care costs are putting pressure on household budgets. For many Americans, the economy is not an abstract political debate but a daily calculation about how to pay bills, fill the refrigerator and cover medical expenses.The poll also reveals a significant change in which party voters trust to manage the economy. 

For the first time in more than a decade, Democrats have moved ahead of Republicans on this issue. That shift could complicate the Republican campaign, which has traditionally relied on its reputation for economic management and fiscal discipline. 

Foreign policy is adding another layer of uncertainty. Trump’s handling of the war with Iran has become a source of public dissatisfaction, with voters concerned about the consequences of the conflict and its impact on energy prices. 

The combination of military tensions and rising living costs is creating a difficult environment for an administration seeking to convince Americans that its policies are working.The broader mood is equally troubling for the president. 

According to the survey, 72% of Americans believe the country is heading in the wrong direction, a five-point increase since April. Meanwhile, 63% of respondents hold an unfavorable view of the Republican Party. These figures suggest that dissatisfaction extends beyond the president himself and could affect Republican candidates in competitive congressional districts.

Trump’s political image is also facing scrutiny. A majority of Americans surveyed consider him too extreme, while 66% believe he is using the presidency to benefit himself financially. Such perceptions could further weaken the administration’s appeal among independent voters and some Americans who supported Trump in 2024.

Still, national polling does not determine the outcome of individual races. Congressional elections are decided district by district, and the Senate map presents a different set of challenges from the House of Representatives.

For Republicans, the immediate challenge is to persuade voters that the administration can address the cost of living and restore confidence in its leadership. 

Democrats, meanwhile, must turn their polling advantage into actual votes and demonstrate that their own economic proposals can deliver tangible improvements. 

Whether that discontent translates into a major shift in congressional power will become clear on November 3.

🔖 Australia proposes new crypto exchange rules for 2027 

📣 Australia has proposed new rules for cryptocurrency trading and custody platforms on October 15, 2026, with financial regulator ASIC seeking public feedback by November 27 before the country’s digital asset licensing framework takes effect in April 2027. 

📊 The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) announced the consultation alongside Consultation Paper 392, which outlines planned requirements for customer asset protection, trading practices and financial resources. The regulator expects to publish final guidance in March 2027, giving businesses time to prepare for the new licensing requirements. Australia’s upcoming rules will bring more cryptocurrency businesses under the country’s existing financial services licensing framework.

⚡️ The Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 creates two regulated categories: digital asset platforms and tokenized custody platforms. Digital asset platforms hold digital tokens for customers and provide related services, while tokenized custody platforms use digital tokens to record customers’ rights to underlying assets.
